I did not use them; every capture cited here is my own, under /private/tmp/opus55/critic/driving-C2/.. Judge: B wins all four pairs clearly; none was close enough to call indistinguishable. The A frames come from one in-development game. It has a coherent art direction (Singapore-style shophouse streets, warm late-afternoon haze, sensible atmospheric perspective) and pair 4 A is its best frame, but the same failures appear in every frame. (1) Life and density: streets and junctions have almost no traffic and no pedestrians. (2) Hero-car shading: the paint is grainy and matte, with weak specular and rim response under a sun ahead of the camera, while B's cars have glossy clear-coat reflections and chrome. (3) Shadows: they are crushed to near-black with little sky or bounce fill, so the bottom third of the frame loses texture. (4) Roads: surfaces are flat and uniform with no cracks, patches, debris or worn paint. (5) Placeholders and repetition: a blank white stop sign, an untextured grey slab, a duplicate player-car model, a skyline of tiled-window boxes and a barren dirt lot. (6) HUD: the minimap is an empty grid, a pistol ammo counter shows while driving, and the '[E] Exit vehicle' prompt sits in the centre of the screen. (7) Composition: the camera is always the same static, centred chase view, against B's low, tilted, motion-blurred angles. Highest-value fixes, in order: populate traffic and pedestrians at junctions; fix vehicle clear-coat, reflection and rim lighting; lift shadow ambient fill; add road wear decals; remove every placeholder prop. Two caveats for the workflow. First, B in pairs 1, 3 and 4 carries a visible game-title logo watermark, which partly unblinds the comparison. I judged on rendered content and would give the same verdicts with the logo cropped. Second, the B frames are curated marketing stills with no HUD, while the A frames are live gameplay captures with HUD. That favours B on composition, but the gaps in density, materials and placeholders hold regardless.
